criteria.text: Link iodine production to Fe(III) reduction rather than merely to iron colour.
criteria.evidence: Ledger (step 3, v0): reaction_occurred 2Fe3+ + 2I- -> 2Fe2+ + I2; Fe2+ 3.94221e-4, Fe3+ 5.7785e-6, I2(ox) 1.97111e-4, I- 6.05779e-4; dFe(II)=3.9422e-4 = 2 x dI2 (exact). Ideal check with the engine's own I2(aq)/I- couple (E0 0.621 vs 0.771 V, logK~5.07): Q=1.05e5 -> ledger is at equilibrium. BUT the same step's reported PHREEQC solution (pe 11.40, redox block, species list) splits Fe as Fe(II) 0.0028932 mol/kg x 0.0997 kg = 2.885e-4 mol and Fe(III) 1.1155e-4 mol (FeSO4+ 8.69e-4 m, Fe+3 1.06e-4 m, ...), contains no I2/I3-, i.e. 28% of iron still ferric vs 1.4% in the ledger; electron books in that view: Fe(II) 2.885e-4 vs 2xI2 3.942e-4 (27% deficit). The UV-vis refusal (step 9) is generated from this Fe(III)-rich speciation. Two reported observables disagree on the very quantity the criterion links.

Real chemistry agrees on bench time: Fe2+ oxygenation at pH<3 is negligibly slow (Singer & Stumm, Science 167 (1970) 1121) and E0(Fe3+/Fe2+) is not exceeded by sulfate kinetically.

criteria.text: What does a melting-point instrument report for a PE/PP mixture?
criteria.evidence: Pure references now return sourced equilibrium Tm (PE 141.45 C = 414.6 K, PP 187.55 C = 460.7 K; Gaur & Wunderlich, JPCRD 10 (1981) 119 and 1051) with 'real grades melt below' boundary - correct. The blend reading claims as 'a law': 'a mixture melts below its lowest-melting pure component and over a range'. PE and isotactic PP are immiscible in the melt and crystallise separately; blends show two melting endotherms close to each pure component (Teh, Rudin & Keung, Adv. Polym. Technol. 13 (1994) 1), so the PP phase does not melt below PE's Tm. The engine applies freezing-point depression (which presumes miscibility) - exactly the miscibility claim the forecast forbids.

criteria.text: Account for additions and losses.
Distinguish unsupported observables from negatives.
criteria.evidence: Heating 300 J now emits typed labels that PE and PP melting are not modelled (fixed). But the thermometer then reports 193.89 C as a measurement: 300 J was charged entirely as sensible heat (1.776 J/K for 1 g). Real: ~2 J/(g K) to reach the PE melt (~230 J) plus PE fusion (~0.5 g x ~150-180 J/g at typical crystallinity) exceeds 300 J, so the blend would sit at or below ~140 C. The temperature reading depends on the unmodelled latent heat yet carries no not_yet_modeled qualifier.

formal.limitations: Polymer melting and fusion enthalpy unmodelled (labelled); blend phase behaviour asserted by colligative rule.
formal.doubts: Reviewer 2: the depression rule may be generic code for any 'mixture' verdict; for immiscible polymers it is wrong in direction of magnitude (no depression of the higher-melting phase).

criteria.text: Can tert-butanol and isopropanol be distinguished by a low-temperature phase test?
criteria.evidence: At 15 C tBuOH is solid, IPA liquid. Lookups: mp 25.82 C (Oetting 1963: 298.97 K) vs -88.48 C; bp 82.35 vs 82.35 C (355.5 K both, NIST WebBook AVG; lit. 82.4/82.3) - boiling non-discriminating, melting decisive. Heating 400 J: tBuOH 288.15 -> 298.97 K using 159.55 J, then 0.035888 of 0.067455 mol melts on the plateau with the remaining 240.45 J -> implied dHfus 6.700 kJ/mol (lit. 6.70 kJ/mol, Oetting 1963). IPA 288.15 -> 319.74 K (Cp 152.2 J/mol K; lit. liquid ~155-156).

criteria.evidence: tBuOH solid 0.0315673 + liquid 0.0358882 = 0.0674554 (added 0.0674554); IPA 0.0832002 unchanged; no evaporation.

The engine's own inspect of the post-extraction aqueous phase shows 87% of the residual 8.27e-6 as I3- (K3=698, [I-]~0.01 M), i.e. free I2 1.04e-6 mol (1.05e-5 M) against 7.0e-3 M in 13.1 mL hexane: implied partition ~670, 8x its stated K. With I3- formation D = 85/(1+698x0.0099) ~ 10.7, so ~58% (5.8e-5 mol) should extract. The control receiver number is wrong by ~+58%. K=85 provenance is an A-level exam question, not a primary measurement.

formal.observed_result: Thiosulfate-reduced iodine (all I-) gives an iodine-free hexane extract; the unreduced control is reported to transfer 91.7% of 1e-4 mol I2 into 0.1 mol hexane.
formal.limitations: Extraction uses a constant K for I2 only; triiodide equilibrium is ignored during partition.
formal.doubts: The comparative inequality survives any K; rejection is for the quantitative control value and internal inconsistency (stated K vs implied 670). Iodine in hexane is phase-tagged 'aqueous' (cosmetic).
formal.adversarial: refuted: Implied K 670 vs stated 85; expected ~58% not 91.7% extraction.
